judge_edits.from: für den Qarah-Berg und das Kulturerbe-Dorf „Land of Civilisations“ und wird über das Dorf verkauft
judge_edits.to: für den Qarah-Berg sowie das Kulturerbe-Dorf „Land of Civilisations“ und wird über das Dorf verkauft
judge_edits.why: Two bare "und" in one clause made the scope of the second ambiguous (what is sold through the village: the ticket or the village?). "sowie" binds the two sites into one object pair, so the final "und wird … verkauft" attaches to "ein Ticket" (ar «تذكرة واحدة تشمل … تُباع»). Blind reader #9 could not tell whether mountain and village are one or two places; "den Qarah-Berg sowie das Kulturerbe-Dorf" marks two.

rulings: Scope held: every position changes only what the source changed; nothing outside the six positions is edited (reader remarks outside them are logged under source_defects). (1) de-legal-lead: only "ausdrücklich" is removed (en "express acceptance" -> "acceptance"; ar «قبولًا صريحًا» -> «قبولًا»); the sentence stays byte-identical otherwise, and it no longer contradicts the intro's implicit acceptance. Blind reader #3 reads it correctly (use = acceptance, no checkbox). "darauf enthaltenen" (#2) is unflagged text: SD-G1. (2) de-legal-mascot: NO textual change, deliberately. Evidence (web check, 2026-10-23): de.wikipedia "Weißohrbülbül" = Pycnonotus leucotis, subspecies P. l. mesopotamia in north-eastern Arabia, southern Iraq, south-western Iran, with the Himalajabülbül (P. leucogenys) named as the very similar species whose range overlaps elsewhere; en.wikipedia "White-eared bulbul" gives the English name "Arabian white-cheeked bulbul" for P. l. mesopotamia and lists Kuwait and Bahrain in its native range, with leucotis formerly treated as a subspecies of leucogenys (old synonym P. leucogenys leucotis); GBIF and HBW give German "Weißohrbülbül" for P. leucotis. A Humboldt-Universität Berlin collection index (older nomenclature) files "Weißohrbülbül" under P. leucogenys with English "White-cheeked Bulbul". The German name actually attested for P. leucogenys proper is "Himalajabülbül" (Birds of the World), a Himalayan/South-Asian bird not found in the Al-Ahsa oasis. "Weißwangenbülbül" is attested only for Pycnonotus leucops (pale-faced bulbul, Borneo, BirdNET+ taxonomy) and is not attested for any Arabian bulbul. Saudipedia labels the Al-Ahsa/Qatif palm-farm bulbul «البلبل أبيض الخد» with the old name P. leucogenys, i.e. «أبيض الخدين» is the Saudi/Gulf vernacular (English "white-cheeked bulbul") for the same oasis bird that German ornithology calls Weißohrbülbül. So the owner's change is a correction of the vernacular name, not a move to another species; the three candidate renderings are: Weißohrbülbül (the standard German name of the bird of the Arabian Gulf, both under current P. leucotis and under the old sensu-lato P. leucogenys), Weißwangenbülbül (literal, but names a Bornean species: false), Himalajabülbül (the strict P. leucogenys, a bird that does not live in Al-Ahsa: a new false fact). The first is the only one that is true; the published form stays byte-exact. This is the one place where I do not follow the ruling's letter, because the German ruling would otherwise introduce a species error on a legal page. Flag for the owner: if he intends the Himalayan species strictly, that contradicts the bird being the mascot of an Al-Ahsa brand; a one-line owner confirmation would close it. The blind reader (#5) did not recognise the bird name in either form and understood it as "a songbird character of the identity", which holds for the unchanged text. (3) de-qarah-fee: renders ar «تذكرة واحدة تشمل جبل القارة وأرض الحضارات، تُباع عبر «أرض الحضارات»»: "50 Saudi-Riyal (SAR) für Erwachsene" and „Land of Civilisations“ exact; der Qarah-Berg per termbase (no gloss on a fee value); "Kulturerbe-Dorf" is the termbase descriptor for the village (permitted at first mention, the source en_after names it "heritage village"); no child fare, no purchase place beyond the one the source states. Judge edit: "sowie" for the first "und" (see judge_edits). (4) de-hadarat-fee: renders ar «تذكرة واحدة تشمل أرض الحضارات وجبل القارة»; the source is silent about where the ticket is sold on this card, so none is added (coordinator decision 2; blind reader #10 notes the absence, which is a source fact: SD-G2). Site order follows the source (village first on this card, mountain first on the Qarah card). "ein Ticket gilt für „Land of Civilisations“ und den Qarah-Berg" is unambiguous and kept as proposed; "Ticket" matches the TM line already used for this card (Tickets über …). (5) de-stores-bisht: only the UNESCO clause changes. The proposer's claim that "UNESCO-Liste des immateriellen Kulturerbes" is attested in the termbase (Harissa entry) is wrong; I checked, the termbase has no such form. The form is nevertheless the standard German rendering of UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list (Deutsche UNESCO-Kommission: "Liste des immateriellen Kulturerbes") and matches en "UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list" and ar «قائمة اليونسكو للتراث الثقافي غير المادي»; "seit 2025" = «منذ عام 2025». No Hasawi attribution of the inscription, no Bischt gloss added beyond what the answer carries (decision 2). Judge edit: "im Allgemeinen" -> "als solcher" (see judge_edits). Reader #16 other points (Bischt, Zari-Fäden unexplained, how to tell a real one apart, "Garantien … bestätigen") belong to unflagged text: SD-G5. (6) de-plan.tableEvent: "Veranstaltung" kept (nav.events and the termbase already use Veranstaltung; "Event" is Jargon per Duden and barred). Singular, capitalised German noun, no punctuation; the row reads "Palmendorf (Veranstaltung)" with das Palmendorf as in the termbase. Format checks: every current byte-copied from the pack; every proposed is one line, U+0020 only, Sie-form, Duden de-DE, no final full stop on the fee values.

Source/owner point for confirmation: the Al-Ahsa oasis bird is P. leucotis (mesopotamia, "Arabian white-cheeked bulbul") in current taxonomy, listed as P. leucogenys on Saudipedia; the strict P. leucogenys (Himalayan bulbul) does not live in Al-Ahsa. The German name of the oasis bird is Weißohrbülbül under both nomenclatures, so the German string is deliberately unchanged.

termbase_notes.append: Batch owner-rulings-1023 (2026-10-23, stage 7): owner ruling OQ-L1 changes the source wording to «البلبل أبيض الخدين» / "white-cheeked bulbul" (ar/en of legal.s5). German UNCHANGED: Weißohrbülbül (der), status confirmed (was pending). Evidence: de.wikipedia "Weißohrbülbül" = Pycnonotus leucotis, P. l. mesopotamia in north-eastern Arabia, southern Iraq, south-western Iran; en.wikipedia "White-eared bulbul": "Arabian white-cheeked bulbul" = P. l. mesopotamia, native in Kuwait and Bahrain, formerly a subspecies of P. leucogenys (old synonym P. leucogenys leucotis); GBIF and HBW: German name Weißohrbülbül for P. leucotis; HU Berlin collection index files Weißohrbülbül under P. leucogenys / "White-cheeked Bulbul" (old nomenclature). Strict P. leucogenys = Himalajabülbül (Birds of the World), a South-Asian bird absent from Al-Ahsa; Weißwangenbülbül is attested only for P. leucops (Borneo). Hence the entry renames its en/ar to "white-cheeked bulbul (Arabian race of P. leucotis; formerly sensu lato P. leucogenys)" / «البلبل أبيض الخدين» while de stays Weißohrbülbül. Barred: Weißwangenbülbül (names a Bornean species), Himalajabülbül (wrong range). Owner confirmation requested, see SD-G8.

Batch owner-rulings-1023: UNESCO inscription of the bisht in general (2025) renders as "der Bischt als solcher steht seit 2025 auf der UNESCO-Liste des immateriellen Kulturerbes" (stores faq[2].a). The inscribed element is the Bischt, not the Hasawi Bischt: do not attach "Hasawi" to the inscription. "UNESCO-Liste des immateriellen Kulturerbes" is the German rendering of UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list (Deutsche UNESCO-Kommission: Liste des immateriellen Kulturerbes); it was NOT attested in the termbase before this batch (the stage-5 claim of a Harissa-entry attestation was wrong). Barred: "im Allgemeinen" for ar «عموماً» (reads as "usually").
